summary: Accepted the beneficiary relationship from nearshoring and friendshoring manufacturing capacity to Ternium with medium positive sensitivity and medium confidence. Current SEC-filed evidence shows a direct path through Pesquería capacity investment and downstream ramp-up, while the revised early-2027 DRI-EAF startup, undisclosed utilization and returns, working-capital absorption, steel cyclicality, non-Mexican exposures, and adverse valuation remain explicit limits. Updated the relationship page, catalog, log, and canonical relationship row; no strategy or follow-up operation was created.

evidence.claim: Ternium's SEC-filed Q1 2026 results report USD 406 million of capex mainly for Pesquería, downstream cold-rolling and galvanizing facilities entering ramp-up, USD 217 million of operating cash flow after a USD 233 million working-capital build, and USD 327 million of net cash. This supports direct regional-capacity exposure while showing material cash-conversion and balance-sheet counterweights.

Ternium's SEC-filed 8 July 2026 sustainability update says the Pesquería DRI-EAF steel shop was expected to begin operations in early 2027, later than the Q1 target of before year-end 2026. The later primary disclosure establishes schedule slippage and keeps commissioning an explicit catalyst and invalidation gate.

The maintained security review records a USD 47.74 paper mark, bounded 48.9% downside and 8.7% base-case downside scenarios, and baseline eligibility only; schedule, unproven capacity returns, cash conversion, cyclicality, valuation, and timing block strategy research.

The maintained idea defines the causal channel from regional manufacturing qualification to local materials demand and requires operating plants, utilization, margins, free cash flow, workable USMCA rules, and adequate infrastructure rather than relying on announcement counts.
